rule.description: A trait merges the single-command identity capability with the child-command collection/discovery capability over one shared metadata type: it requires, on one interface, an associated item producing a single X and an associated item producing many X. Every implementor must then provide every capability group whichever role it plays, and every generic function bounded by the trait depends on capability groups it may never use. Detection is structural; trait, member, and metadata type names are never matched against fixed lists.

checks.description: One trait declares both the single-command identity capability and the child-command collection/discovery capability over the same command metadata type.
checks.detected_relation: trait definition -> identity capability member + collection/discovery capability member over one shared metadata type
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds every implementor's dependency boundary: no role in the command tree needs all of the merged capability groups.

matches.evidence: trait `CommandSpec` (spanning the former TopLevelCommand, SubCommands, and SubCommand interfaces) requires COMMANDS: one child-command list, COMMAND: one command identity, and dynamic_commands: runtime-discovered child commands, all over CommandInfo.

checks.description: Every impl of the merged interface must provide all capability groups whichever role the implementing type actually plays.
checks.detected_relation: impl of merged interface -> obligation to provide unused capability groups
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Implementors are forced to synthesize placeholder members for capabilities that belong to other command-tree roles.

matches.evidence: The blanket impl for boxed subcommands forwards COMMANDS, COMMAND, and dynamic_commands even though the boxing pattern only needs identity forwarding.

checks.description: Generic functions whose type parameter is bounded by the merged interface but whose bodies use none of its members.
checks.detected_relation: generic function bound -> merged interface members never used by the function body
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The bound drags the full merged capability surface into call sites that only need argument parsing.

matches.evidence: `pub fn try_from_env<T: CommandSpec>()` never reads COMMANDS, COMMAND, or dynamic_commands; parsing only uses FromArgs behavior.
`pub fn from_env<T: CommandSpec>()` delegates to try_from_env and never uses any merged member.
`pub fn cargo_from_env<T: CommandSpec>()` never uses any merged member.

supporting_changes.description: Derive codegen implements the merged interface for every derived type: top-level structs receive placeholder command identities, subcommand structs and enums get collection members re-declared through the same interface, and help/missing-requirement rendering reads collections through it. These sites propagate the merged interface rather than being direct matches of the trait-shape rule.

excluded.reason: Capability members (from_args, redact_arg_values) all produce single values; no collection capability over a shared metadata type.
Runtime command discovery only (a collection of command metadata plus differently-typed members); it declares no single-command identity capability.
Capabilities are declared over distinct metadata types (command info with args vs subcommand info), not one shared type.
Single capability (generating one completion document); no identity/collection pair.
